memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But if you will not listen to me and carry out all these commands, and
if you reject my decrees and abhor my laws and fail to carry out all my
commands and so violate my covenant, then I will do this to you'"
- Lev 26:14-16a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter now turns. Having described the blessings of faithfulness,
God warns of the consequences of turning away. These are sobering words,
and we should not soften them.

Notice first that this is covenant language. Israel had freely entered
into an agreement with God, and these warnings spelled out what breaking
that agreement would mean for the nation. This is not God being harsh or
unpredictable; it is God being honest about the real consequences of
abandoning Him.

We should be careful here. These specific national consequences belonged
to Israel's covenant. We should not read every hardship in a believer's
life as God's punishment for sin — Scripture explicitly warns against that
(John 9:2-3; Job's friends were wrong). Suffering in this fallen world has
many causes.

Yet a lasting truth remains: turning away from God has real consequences,
because sin is not harmless. God's warnings are never the words of a
tyrant looking for reasons to punish. They are the words of a loving
Father telling His children the truth about the cliff edge ahead.

Dear reader, love warns. A parent who lets a child walk towards danger
without a word does not love them. Hebrews reminds us that the Lord
disciplines those He loves (Heb 12:6). Warnings are a mercy.

Do not resent God's warnings. Receive them as the voice of One who loves
you too much to stay silent.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I receive God's warnings as love or resent them as harshness?
2. Where might God be lovingly warning me about a path I am on?
3. Am I wrongly reading my hardships as God's punishment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your warnings flow from love, not cruelty. Give me
a soft heart to hear them, and turn me back whenever I begin to drift.
Amen.
